title: Field-extension descent for finite-type schemes carrying an ample module
statement: Let $k\subseteq L$ be an arbitrary extension of fields [def-weil-field, def-pc-field-extension], and let $X'$ be a finite-type $L$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $X'$ carries an ample invertible $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module [def-sc-invertible-module, def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. Every descent datum on $X'$ relative to $\operatorname{Spec}L\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-pd-descent-datum] is effective: there exist a $k$-scheme $X$ and an $L$-isomorphism $X\times_kL\simeq X'$ inducing the given datum [def-pc-base-change]. The ample module is not required to carry a descent datum. No algebraicity, separability or finite-degree assumption on $L/k$ is imposed.

source.place: BLR 6.5 Theorem 1 proof, first paragraph, printed p.160 (PDF p.166): limit reduction to a finite extension, radicial and finite Galois descent, and the affine-neighbourhood criterion; BLR 6.2 Example B. The argument only uses finite type and an ample module, not the group law. Local PDF WANTED; primary scan read online.

proof.text: We first check coverings that will occur below. For any nonzero $k$-algebra $A$, the field-algebra lemma makes $k\to A$ faithfully flat. The ring-to-scheme flatness criterion and faithful-flat spectrum surjectivity make $\operatorname{Spec}A\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ flat and surjective. Its source is affine, so the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A$ verifies the affine-cover condition in the definition of an fpqc covering. This applies to $A=L$, to every $k$-subalgebra $C\subseteq L$, and to every residue field of such a $C$.

source.place: Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful), covering hypotheses; algebra.tex Tag 04VV, field-algebra faithful flatness.

proof.text: Prove first the finite-extension case, for an arbitrary finite field extension $E/k$ and an $E$-scheme $V$ with an ample invertible module and a descent datum. A finite $k$-basis of $E$ generates it as a module and also as an algebra. The affine-local-target criterion and the definition of a finite morphism therefore make $p:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ finite. The field $k$ is Noetherian (its only ideals are $0,k$); the finite-type-algebra finite-presentation lemma makes $E$ finitely presented over $k$. Thus $p$ is locally of finite presentation by the affine definition. Step 1 supplies flatness and surjectivity. The ample finite-set lemma puts every finite subset of $V$ inside an affine open. Apply invariant-affine neighbourhoods to this datum and $p$: every point has a transport-invariant affine neighbourhood over an affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}k$. The invariant-affine gluing theorem now makes the datum effective. This proves the finite-extension case without separability or a datum on the ample module.

source.place: Tags 0H8K (lemma-descend-along-finite-with-bound) and 03JE (lemma-find-invariant-affine); properties.tex Tag 01ZY; descent.tex Tags 0245 and 0AP4. Finite-locally-free invariant-affine version of the finite-extension argument in BLR 6.5, p.160.

proof.text: Return to $X'/L$. A field is Noetherian since each ideal is either zero or the whole field, so $\operatorname{Spec}L$ is Noetherian. Finite-type preservation of Noetherianness makes $X'$ Noetherian; locally Noetherian quasi-separatedness makes it quasi-separated. On a finite affine finite-type cover, the finite-type-algebra finite-presentation lemma gives finitely presented $L$-algebras. The structure morphism $X'\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is quasi-compact by the definition of finite type, and quasi-separated by qcqs morphism permanence (1), because its source $X'$ is quasi-separated. Hence $X'\to\operatorname{Spec}L$ is locally of finite presentation, quasi-compact and quasi-separated, that is, of finite presentation. This checks the input to spreading out; finite type alone over a general base would not suffice.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), checking its finite-presentation hypothesis; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6.

proof.text: Let $I$ be the inclusion-ordered set of finitely generated $k$-subalgebras $C\subseteq L$. It is small in the universe of $L$, nonempty (it contains $k$), and directed: adjoining both finite sets of generators gives a common upper bound. Its union is $L$, since any element lies in the subalgebra it generates. The affine-limit theorem identifies $\operatorname{Spec}L$ with $\varprojlim_C\operatorname{Spec}C$. All stages are affine and hence qcqs, and all transition maps are affine by the affine-local-target criterion. Apply clause (1) of spreading out to obtain a finitely presented $Y_0\to\operatorname{Spec}C_0$ and a specified $L$-isomorphism $(Y_0)_L\simeq X'$. For $C\supseteq C_0$ put $Y_C=(Y_0)_C$. These schemes are qcqs with affine transition maps, and have limit $X'$: the universal property of the fibre product identifies compatible maps to the $Y_C$ with a map to $Y_0$ and a compatible family of maps to the $\operatorname{Spec}C$.

source.place: Tags 01YW (lemma-affine), 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (1); BLR 6.5 proof, printed p.160, limit reduction.

proof.text: Apply invertible-module limit descent to $X'=\varprojlim_{C\supseteq C_0}Y_C$ and the given ample module $M'$ to obtain an invertible module $M_{C_1}$ whose pullback is $M'$. Apply ample-module limit descent to this module on the same tail system. After increasing $C_1$ to $C_2$, its pullback $M_{C_2}$ is ample on $Y_{C_2}$. Any later enlargement still has an ample module, by relative ample base change: apply the relative-ample affine-cover criterion to the singleton cover of $\operatorname{Spec}C_2$. Its quasi-compactness hypothesis holds because $Y_{C_2}$ is finitely presented over this base. Then apply relative ample base change and take the whole later affine base as its affine open. No datum on $M'$ or on any $M_C$ has been used or constructed.

We descend the scheme datum itself, retaining the ample model from step 5. For $n=2,3$, the rings $C^{\otimes_k n}$ have colimit $L^{\otimes_k n}$: maps out of these colimits are compatible $n$-tuples of $k$-algebra maps out of the $C$, equivalently $n$-tuples of maps out of $L$, which is the tensor-product universal property. Taking a tail $C\supseteq C_2$ leaves the colimit unchanged. The affine-limit theorem supplies the corresponding inverse limits of spectra. Over $\operatorname{Spec}(C^{\otimes_k2})$, the two pullbacks of $Y_C$ are of finite presentation, being base changes of $Y_0$. Apply clause (2) of spreading out separately to the given datum isomorphism $\varphi$ over $L\otimes_kL$ and to its inverse. Directedness puts both descended maps $a,b$ over a common $C$. Their composites pull back to the identities; two applications of clause (3), followed by a common enlargement of $C$, make $ba=1$ and $ab=1$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism with precisely the prescribed pullback $\varphi$.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clauses (2) and (3), applied over the double tensor base; descent.tex Tag 023V (definition-descent-datum).

proof.text: Over the triple tensor base $\operatorname{Spec}(C^{\otimes_k3})$, compare the two maps $a_{02}$ and $a_{12}a_{01}$. Their domains and codomains are pullbacks of $Y_C$, hence of finite presentation. Their pullbacks to $\operatorname{Spec}(L^{\otimes_k3})$ agree by the given cocycle. Clause (3) of spreading out gives a further $C$ on which $a_{02}=a_{12}a_{01}$. The inverse equations persist under base change. We now have a finitely presented scheme $Y_C/C$, an ample invertible module on it, and a genuine descent datum $D_C$ relative to $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ whose pullback to $L$ is the original datum. In particular the limit argument has descended the equations, not just the underlying isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01ZM (lemma-descend-finite-presentation), clause (3), over the triple tensor base; descent.tex Tag 023V.

proof.text: Choose a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of the nonzero finitely generated $k$-algebra $C$, and put $E=C/\mathfrak m$. Zariski's lemma says $E/k$ is finite. Pull back $Y_C,D_C$ along $h:\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. The singleton affine-cover criterion, followed by relative ample base change, gives an ample module on $Y_E$; $Y_C/C$ is finitely presented, so is quasi-compact as required by that criterion. The finite-extension case of step 2 makes $D_E$ effective. Both $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ are singleton fpqc covers by step 1, and their triangle with $h$ commutes. The square defining $Y_E$ is cartesian, and its datum is the pullback of $D_C$. Apply fpqc refinement reflection of effectivity to deduce that $D_C$ is effective. This theorem does not require $h$ itself to be flat. Let $X/k$ and $X_C\simeq Y_C$ realize $D_C$. Base changing this isomorphism along $C\subseteq L$ gives $X_L\simeq X'$; its datum is the prescribed one because $D_C$ was descended together with $\varphi$ and its cocycle. This is exactly effectivity as defined, for the original arbitrary extension $L/k$.

source.place: Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful), refinement reflection of effectivity; algebra.tex Tag 00FV (theorem-nullstellensatz), part (1); BLR 6.5 proof, printed p.160, specialization to a finite residue extension.
